findings.title: Single-droplet, single-instance runtime is a hard SPOF
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: topology is still one droplet with one api/worker/web instance (infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml; infra/terraform/digitalocean/droplet.tf:1-15) and the deploy now uses a per-service rolling recreate plus an in-place caddy force-recreate/zero-downtime refresh (deploy-do.yml:1027-1050), which removes the planned-outage part of the finding. Host loss remains a full outage; documented as an accepted single point of failure in docs/PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:11-13. Owner/budget decision.

findings.title: API defaults to the service-role DB client (RLS bypass)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: getScopedClient still returns the service-role client for modules not in the allow-list (services/supabase.ts:197-224) and the per-module rollout is owner-gated (docs/RLS-rollout.md). Mitigations verified: production refuses to boot with an empty RLS_READS_ENABLED (lib/rls-startup-check.ts:26-55, called from main.ts:14) and every bypass/enforcement is metered (metrics.ts:175-197, services/supabase.ts:223).

findings.title: Prometheus loads rules but has no alert routing
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: prometheus.yml:14-17 alerting targets alertmanager:9093, the alertmanager service renders via infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml with critical/default/ntfy receivers and an external Watchdog route, and prod deploys fail closed when the watchdog URL is unset (deploy-do.yml:845-863). promtool check rules: 26 rules SUCCESS; rule tests SUCCESS.

findings.title: API always enqueues to BullMQ while the worker backend is a separate setting with no parity check
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: both deployables read the shared QUEUE_BACKEND value (infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:21; api/config/env.ts:95,156-167 refuses non-bullmq in production; worker/env.ts:32,81-91 enforces the same), the API refuses to enqueue on a mismatch even outside production (lib/task-producer.ts:100-111), and both export the resolved backend as a metric (api/lib/metrics.ts:306-318).

findings.title: One non-replicated Redis backs queue, cache, idempotency and scan locks; failure degrades silently
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the silence is fixed - degradation is metered (api/lib/metrics.ts:330-338, worker/redis-failures.ts) and alerted (prometheus.rules.yml:390-455 MCTWorkerQueueDisconnected + mct-redis-degradation) with a runbook (docs/PLATFORM_FAILURE_RUNBOOKS.md:55-90). Remaining: Redis is still a single non-replicated instance (48 MB cap, RDB-only, compose redis service) with no replication/maxmemory policy, so an OOM kill loses queue/lock/idempotency state; replication/splitting is an infra decision.

findings.title: Web middleware gates routes on an unverified JWT `exp`
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: unchanged by design and explicitly documented as a non-authoritative UX gate - the module docstring states a forged-but-unexpired cookie reaches only the page shell and every server component re-checks via the API (apps/web/middleware.ts:4-16). Residual accepted (the API verifies signatures); an assertion/test that no data access relies on isAuthenticated is still absent.

findings.title: Architecture diagram and ADR 004 contradict the as-built runtime
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAM.md documents API_INTERNAL_URL (:78,137) and the rolling recreate (:161) and now includes node-exporter (:59,116); docs/adr/README.md marks 004 superseded by 012 (:23) and contains the ADR 012 body (:147).

findings.title: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` runtime override is inert for server-side code; docs claim internal SSR routing
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: server-side code reads API_INTERNAL_URL at request time (apps/web/lib/api.ts:11-15) and compose sets it to http://api:4000 (infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:242); the diagram documents the same.

findings.title: Request timeout returns 408 but never cancels the handler
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: middleware/request-timeout.ts aborts a per-request AbortSignal (exported via getRequestAbortSignal) and destroys the socket after the 408 flushes; wired at app.ts.

findings.title: Worker metrics/health are unauthenticated while the API gates /metrics
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the worker /metrics endpoint enforces a constant-time bearer token and 404s when METRICS_TOKEN is unset (apps/worker/src/health-server.ts:12-40,77-84), matching the API; prometheus.yml scrapes with the token file (docker-compose.yml:270-278).

findings.title: Host-resource alerting has no liveness rule for the new node-exporter
findings.note: NEW at 6b7aa1a5: prometheus.yml:47-53 adds the node-exporter job and prometheus.rules.yml:459-505 adds disk/memory alerts, but the only target-down rule is `up{job=~"mct-api|mct-worker"} == 0` (prometheus.rules.yml:11-20). If node-exporter stops being scraped (image/config failure, network isolation, collector crash), all host-resource alerts silently go absent while Alertmanager and the Watchdog stay green; the container health gate in deploy-do.yml:1070 only covers deploy-time container health. Add `up{job="node-exporter"} == 0` (or absent(node_...)) with service-availability severity so the loss of the only host signal pages.

report: Read-only re-verification at 6b7aa1a5. 6/10 previous ARCH findings are verified fixed, 4 remain partially fixed (ARCH-P2-001, P2-002, P2-005, P3-001), 0 regressed. This diff adds host metrics (node-exporter plus disk/memory alerts) and refreshes the proxy last with an in-place caddy recreate; the single-droplet, single-Redis and service-role-default architecture is unchanged and remains owner-gated/accepted. One new P3: the new host-resource alerts have no `up{job="node-exporter"}` liveness rule, so losing the exporter silently removes the only host signal. Executed: promtool check rules against infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml (26 rules SUCCESS) and promtool test rules (SUCCESS); `docker compose -f infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml config` (exit 0); read compose/terraform/prometheus/deploy workflow and the architecture/ADR docs.
